h1: European-style (Amada-Promecam) press brake dies — 1V, multi-V, self-centring, T, hemming and ESH insert dies
intro: EUROSTAMP dies for the European-style (Amada-Promecam) lower beam found on most press brakes sold in Canada. Six families: solid 1V dies from V18 to V220 mm (.71 – 8.66″) for sheet and plate; 2V, 4V and 3U dies that hold several openings in one block, with their holders; slim self-centring 1V dies on rails; T dies — a slim body on a 60 mm foot — for return flanges and closed profiles; mechanical and pneumatic hemming dies that pre-bend and close a hem with one punch; and the ESH insert dies, nitrided all over to 65 HRC. C45 and 42CrMo4 steel, induction-hardened on the V and shoulders, in 835 and 415 mm lengths and 805 mm sectioned sets — with DXF profiles for your CNC.
hero_points: 1V dies V18 – V220 mm (.71 – 8.66″), rated to 67 US t/ft (200 t/m); 2V, 4V and 3U dies with holders

faq.q: How do I choose the V opening?
faq.a: For mild steel up to about 1/2″, start with a V of 8 times the thickness: V16 (5/8″) for 14 gauge, V24 for 1/8″, V50 for 1/4″. Thicker plate needs 10 to 12 times; aluminum can go to 6 times, stainless wants 8 to 10. A wider V needs less force and gives a larger inside radius (about 1/6 of the V) but a longer minimum flange (about 0.7 × V). The tonnage chart and the guide on the press brake tooling overview page work through it.

A 1V die gives the best support and the highest load rating for one thickness, and the solid 60 mm block is the most rigid. A 4V die puts four openings on one 60 mm block — turn it to change the V — so one die covers a range of gauges, which suits job shops that change thickness several times a day. The 2V dies do the same with two openings.

faq.q: What is the difference between a T die and a self-centring die?
faq.a: Both are slim. A T die stands on a 60 mm (2.36″) foot and clamps in the lower beam like any European die; its narrow body leaves room for return flanges. A self-centring die is 14 mm wide and sits on a rail (2058 or 2059) that lines it up under the punch, so changing V openings is quick and needs no alignment.

faq.q: How does a hemming die work?
faq.a: In the first stroke the acute V on top of the die pre-bends the flange to about 30° with an acute or hemming punch; in the second stroke the punch closes on the spring-loaded upper plate and flattens the hem. One die and one punch do both steps without a tool change. The pneumatic (PN) versions open and close on shop air.

faq.q: Can we get the tools as DXF files for our CNC?
faq.a: Yes — every tool in these tables that has a DXF link can be downloaded straight from the page: the profile drawn in millimetres, ready to import into the tool library of a Delem, ESA or Cybelec control or into offline bending software. For the few tools without one, ask us and we get the drawing from EUROSTAMP.
